title: fix(plugin-approvals): the generic data door serves sys_approval_action and sys_approval_approver rows by their request's visibility (#22589)
body:
Fixes #22589
Clause-②: no

## What this does

A read of a request's two child tables through the generic data door (`find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate` on the engine, so the REST data routes, the export route, the MCP data tool and every other engine read) now returns only the rows whose request the approvals door (`/api/v1/approvals/*`) serves the same caller:

- `sys_approval_action`, the decision log (actor, decision, comment text);
- `sys_approval_approver`, the pending-approver index.

This is the sibling half of #22559 (PR #22587, `76bc1e03a3`), which gave `sys_approval_request` the same rule. The default (no grant, `403`) is unchanged.

## Step 1: reach, measured before any code

Measured through the real HTTP data routes on an in-process stack (`@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack` with the real `SecurityPlugin`, automation, the record-change trigger and `ApprovalsServicePlugin`). The scene: one approval flow, two submitters each with one pending request, one position-holding approver, and members granted read on one child table at a time through an app permission set. The probe was a local scratch file and is not part of this PR.

| caller (class) | table read | before (`76bc1e03a3`) | after (`e6d4665bc6`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| member, no grant (control) | either table: list, a request's list, by id | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| member with a read grant, takes part in neither request | `sys_approval_action` | both requests' rows by list (total 2), by another request's pin, and by id (`200`) | 0 rows (total 0); by id `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` |
| same, grant on the other table | `sys_approval_approver` | both requests' rows (total 2); by id `200` | 0 rows; by id `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` |
| submitter of one request, with both grants | either table | the other submitter's rows too (by list and by id) | own request's rows only; the other's by id `404` |
| current approver of both, with both grants | either table | (no grant in the first run) | both requests' rows, each request's Timeline 1 row, by id `200` |

On both runs the approvals door listed 0 requests and 0 history rows for the non-participants, so the generic door was serving rows of requests the approvals door does not show the caller. `sys_approval_token` (a third request-keyed table) had no rows in this scene, so its reach is NOT MEASURED; see the acceptance notes.

## One definition, both doors

- **No second rule.** The child-table gates (`bindRequestChildReadGates`, `request-read-gate.ts`) ask the same in-package source the parent's gate asks, `requestVisibilitySourceOf(service).visibleRequestIdsFor(...)`, which is the approvals door's private `visibleRequestIds`: the participant set, the override actor's unrestricted view (`null`, so administrators and system reads are never narrowed and the answer costs no read), and the default-OFF record-reader tier on top. The gate ANDs a conjunct on `request_id` built only from the ids it returned.
- **Which request a read names** (`requestChildReadTarget`): `request_id` pinned (a record page's Timeline) is the request loaded by id, which carries its own anchor, as `listActions` reads it. `id` pinned (a row read by id) is the row loaded by id: the source resolves the row's request through `findChildRequestId`, which `authorizeFileRead` now shares, so the two doors cannot disagree about which request a row belongs to. Anything else is untargeted, the participant set alone, so the inbox shape is not widened by the tier.
- **The parent's gate and the children's are one binder.** `bindVisibilityGate` (module-private) holds the middleware body; `bindRequestReadGate` keeps its signature and behaviour (keyed on `id`), and the children are keyed on `request_id`. `requestVisibilityFilter` takes the column.
- **Fails closed.** A failed visibility answer denies the read and logs the same warning as the parent's gate, now with the object in its metadata. A row with no request is in no set.
- **Absence, not refusal.** A row the caller may not see answers a by-id read as a missing one does, `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`; a list's `total` and a grouped count are narrowed like its rows.
- **The tier never anchors on a child-table row** (`addRecordReaderVisibleIds`), as it already never anchored on a request. The anchor read runs as the caller, so on a child table it would pass through that table's gate, which asks about the request the row belongs to, whose anchor can be that very row. Ablation B below measures the unbounded re-entry this prevents.
- **Published surface unchanged.** No member is added to `ApprovalService` (its published type is unchanged); `src/index.ts` is untouched; `requestVisibilitySourceOf` stays a module export the package entry does not re-export; no `packages/spec` path. Who may decide is untouched: no decision path is edited.
- Bound in `ApprovalsServicePlugin.start()` beside `bindRequestReadGate`, outside `disableAutoHooks`, as the parent's is. An engine without a middleware seam gets one boot warning naming all three tables.

## The record page's Timeline (the #22567 regression pin)

The request record page lists `sys_approval_action` keyed on `request_id`. Pinned in `request-child-read-gate.integration.test.ts`:

- the submitter, the current approver and an administrator each keep the request's Timeline rows, by the implicit filter and by the filter-array spelling;
- for every caller (non-participant, record reader, both submitters, approver, administrator) and both requests, the Timeline's rows equal `listActions`, tier off and tier on;
- by id, an action row is served exactly when `authorizeFileRead` admits it, tier off and tier on.

## Pins and ablations

New file `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/request-child-read-gate.integration.test.ts`, on the parent's rig: a real ObjectQL engine over better-sqlite3, the real `ApprovalsServicePlugin.start()`, and the real data-door normalizer (`ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.findData` / `getData`). 25 tests: per table, a non-participant sees nothing (list, a request's list, count, grouped count), a hidden row by id answers as a missing one, a participant sees only their own request's rows, an administrator and system reads are unchanged; the Timeline pins above; tier on, per table; fail closed, per table; the re-entry fuse, per table.

- **Red first:** on the unmodified code the new file ran 17 failed and 8 passed. The 8 are the positives and controls: scene, administrator, system, Timeline readers, tier-on readers.
- **Green:** with the fix, both gate files ran 41 passed (25 new and 16 of the parent's).

Ablations, each from the committed head `7721d61e0c` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit x1 to x0, blob changed; restored to the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty, re-proved after each leg by the driver's own trap-armed check). The subject resolves through relative source imports, so no `dist/` is on the path and no rebuild applies. Run on both gate files:

| | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| A | child gates unwired in `approvals-plugin.ts` | 17 failed / 24 passed: every negative pin of both tables, both parity pins, the fail-closed pins and the fuses. First: `expected { ids: [ …(4) ], total: 4 } to deeply equal { ids: [], total: +0 }` |
| B | the tier's anchor guard no longer covers child tables | 2 failed: both fuses, `expected 9 to be 1` (re-entry until the fuse at depth 9) |
| C | the gate's catch fails open | 3 failed: the parent's and both children's fail-closed pins |
| D | a row read by id no longer resolves its request (untargeted) | 3 failed: the tier-on by-id pins for both tables and the tier-on parity pin (`expected null to be 'aact_…'`) |
| E | a read pinned by `request_id` no longer asks the targeted shape | 3 failed: the tier-on request-list pins for both tables and the tier-on parity pin |

With the tier off, the targeted and untargeted answers are identical, so D and E move tier-on pins only. That is the expected direction.

## Verification (head `7721d61e0c`, which merges `origin/main` `d748ae80af`, a spec-only commit)

- `pnpm turbo run build --concurrency=1`: 73 tasks, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 67 files, 988 passed, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` holds 8 files / 324 errors / 27 signatures; the new file adds none.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 67; all 67 ran, each exit 0. `--ran` with recorded exit codes: 67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a derived zero).
- Lint, narrowed: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 4 changed `.ts` files gives 4 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The population is read from `eslint.config.mjs` (`isPathIgnored` false for all four). No `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` is set, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.

## Acceptance notes

- **`sys_approval_token`, same family, not folded in.** It declares `get` / `list` on the generic door with no read middleware, and its rows carry `request_id`, `approver_id`, `token_hash` and `expires_at`. Measured: the control answers `403`; with a grant, `200` with 0 rows, because no action-link token existed in the scene, so its reach is NOT MEASURED. It is left out because who may see token rows is a policy question rather than a mechanical extension: the approvals door serves token rows to nobody, while request visibility would serve them to participants. Reported to the seat.
- **On a default deployment the record page is denied to its declared audience.** No baseline set grants read on the three approval tables, so a request's submitter and approvers get `403` on the request's own data-door read and on its Timeline unless an app grants read. Measured in both probe runs; it predates this PR, and #22559's card measured the request half. With all three tables now narrowed to request visibility, a baseline grant would serve only visible rows. Whether to add one is a product call outside this PR.
- **A row read by id carries the caller's whole visible set** as its `request_id` conjunct (the row's request is resolved inside the source, not in the gate). This is correct but wider in SQL than the parent's one-id by-id conjunct. It is bounded by the participant probes' window (`APPROVER_INDEX_CAP`).
- **`authorizeFileRead` now reads the row's request through `findChildRequestId`**, with a `request_id` projection added and its behaviour unchanged. Its existing tests in `approval-service.test.ts` pass in the full suite.
- **The anchor-guard extension narrows the approvals door too**, only for a deployment that names `sys_approval_action` or `sys_approval_approver` in `recordReaderVisibleObjects`. No in-repo caller does, and the `serve` command passes no options to the plugin.
- Declared to CI: the dogfood suites. They resolve `plugin-approvals` from source; the one dogfood reader of these tables (`position-address-readers`) reads as the system, which is unnarrowed.
